title: Nvidia backs startup developing chiller-free data center cooling system
html:
A startup promising to cut data center cooling bills with a novel chiller-free system has raised $500,000 from backers including Nvidia.

Madrone, which is part of the Y Combinator business incubator program, has raised the cash in a seed round backed by the GPU giant, as well as Y Combinator itself and investment firm Tekedia Capital.

Founded by Akshay Trikha and Erik Meike, Madrone says its modular system will sit outside the data center and supply cool facility water that can be used in servers. It claims it will do this using a thermodynamic process, without the need for the kind of mechanical chillers often found in data center cooling setups.

Precisely how it intends to do this has not been revealed by the company, but it is trumpeting some big potential savings. With up to 30 percent of data center power being dedicated to cooling, Madrone’s thesis is that, by using its system, this power could be redirected to serve the data center’s hardware, giving operators a potential $78 million in additional revenue per 100MW of GPUs per year.

It should be noted that many data centers already choose to eschew mechanical chillers in favor of free cooling, using the ambient air to reduce the temperature of cooling fluid, but this is not practical in hot environments, which is where Madrone is hoping to clean up. The company cites the example of Texas, the second largest data center market in the US, as an area where its system could work particularly well.

Meike has some cooling experience, having previously worked as a thermal engineer at Apple, while Trikha deployed machine learning systems at battery technology firm QuantumScape.

The pair have built a 100kW demonstrator unit, but will need to scale up their technology significantly to enable it to be deployed at data center scale.
summary: Y Combinator venture Madrone secures $500k seed funding
